title: Assembly line vision QC POC - deployment & services proposal (draft)
content:
Purpose and overview:
This draft SOW captures a proposed 8-week Proof-of-Concept (POC) to validate Redwood Inference as the inference platform for on-prem visual quality inspection at Acme Manufacturing's composite assembly line. The goal is to integrate a lightweight camera array, run an object/defect detection model with Redwood Private (on-prem control plane) and Redwood Dedicated fallback in the cloud, and demonstrate end-to-end SLAs for latency, throughput, and model accuracy on a held-out validation set.

High-level success criteria (POC acceptance):
- End-to-end inference latency per image < 120 ms (95th percentile) for single-camera requests under production line load pattern (burst up to 100 req/s across edge gateways).
- True positive rate >= 92% and false positive rate <= 5% on the POC validation dataset defined in Appendix A.
- System handles planned burst scaling without dropping more than 0.1% of requests during 10-minute stress test.
- Integration with Acme MES to emit standardized JSON defect events and a simple dashboard for line operators.
- Handover documentation and runbook delivered; 2-hour knowledge transfer session completed with engineering and operations.

Scope of work (what Redwood will deliver):
1) Discovery & architecture (Week 0-1)
   - 3 workshops (stakeholders, infra, security) to finalize network topology, camera counts, and test dataset curation.
   - Deliver: Architecture diagram, security checklist, and POC test plan.

2) On-prem pilot deployment (Week 2-4)
   - Provide Redwood Private appliance config (container images and operators) for Acme on their existing RHEL hosts.
   - Implement lightweight edge gateway service to aggregate camera frames, perform pre-processing, and batch inference calls to local Redwood runtime.
   - Implement KV/prefix caching for repeated frame contexts as appropriate.

3) Model onboarding & tuning (Week 3-5)
   - Assist in vetting Acme-provided model or onboard an open-model baseline (quantization recommended for throughput).
   - Run 3 rounds of prompt/threshold tuning and small evals against held-out labeled frames.

4) Reliability & fallback integration (Week 4-6)
   - Configure smart routing: local on-prem inference with automatic failover to Redwood Dedicated region for capacity/backups.
   - Setup canary rollout and A/B traffic split tooling for model swaps.

5) Monitoring, dashboards & handover (Week 6-8)
   - Redwood Console dashboards for per-route latency, token-equivalent cost, error rates, and per-model quality regressions against test prompts.
   - Delivery of runbooks, incident playbooks, and 2-hour handover session.

Out of scope (explicit exclusions):
- Development of new custom detection models from scratch (we will tune or onboard provided models).
- Long-term hosting or operational support beyond the POC period (ongoing managed services can be scoped separately).
- Physical camera procurement or electrical/civil work on factory floor.

Assumptions: 
- Acme will provide a labeled validation dataset (min 1,500 frames) and access to a non-production network segment within two weeks of SOW start.
- On-prem hardware meets minimum GPU + NVMe capacity as specified in appendix B; if not, Dedicated fallback will be used and may impact latency results.
- Customer will provide 2 named technical points-of-contact and an environment admin with sudo privileges for install windows.

Security & compliance notes:
- Redwood Private will be deployed into Acme’s VPC/subnet with customer-managed KMS for keys.
- Audit logging enabled with retention of 90 days for POC.
- No customer PII will be ingested as part of the POC unless explicitly authorized; any transfer of real production images requires data handling signoff.

Deliverables:
- Architecture diagram and final POC test plan.
- Deployed Redwood Private POC environment and edge gateway artifacts.
- Model onboarding report (metrics, tuning changes, recommended thresholds).
- Monitoring dashboards, exportable PDF.
- Runbook and incident response playbook.
- Final POC report with measured KPIs and recommended next steps.

Pricing & estimate (draft):
Professional services (fixed-fee POC):
- Discovery & architecture: 24 hours (2 engineers) = 48 engineer-hours
- On-prem deployment & integration: 80 engineer-hours
- Model onboarding & tuning: 64 engineer-hours
- Reliability, testing & failover: 40 engineer-hours
- Dashboards, documentation & handover: 24 engineer-hours
Total estimated engineer-hours: 256 hours
Rate: $225 / engineer-hour (applies to solutions eng team for POC engagements)
Subtotal services: $57,600
Travel & incidental allowance (estimate): $2,000 (virtual-first; in-person optional)
Contingency (10%): $5,960
Total POC professional services (estimate): $65,560

Infrastructure / hosting estimate (optional add-on):
- Redwood Private licensing for POC (30-day eval license): $0 (trial) or $4,000 if extended beyond 30 days.
- If Dedicated Cloud fallback used during POC: estimate 1 x 40GB GPU instance reserved for POC windows = $3,200 (30 days on-demand equivalent); actual billing based on usage.
- Note: production Dedicated/reserved contracts priced separately (example: 4-GPU pool reserved monthly starting at $18k/mo).

Payment milestones (suggested):
- 25% on SOW signature (mobilization)
- 50% mid-POC (end of Week 4, after on-prem deployment & initial tuning)
- 25% on final delivery and acceptance

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0: SOW sign, kickoff, workshop scheduling
- Week 1: Discovery workshops, finalize test plan
- Weeks 2-4: Deploy on-prem POC, edge gateway integration
- Weeks 3-6: Model onboarding, tuning, begin reliability testing
- Weeks 6-8: System validation, dashboarding, handover, final report

Acceptance testing and exit criteria:
- Run full validation test per test plan: 10,000 frames replayed with production load profile and QA labeling.
- KPIs measured and documented; acceptance if success criteria met for latency and accuracy.
- If KPIs are within 5% of targets but not fully met, agreed remediation plan and 2-week extension may be executed (scope and cost to be negotiated).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: On-prem hardware underprovisioned -> Mitigation: Use Redwood Dedicated fallback for stress tests; add quick hardware checklist in discovery workshop.
- Risk: Label quality insufficient for reliable tuning -> Mitigation: Provide labeling guidance and small labeling sprint optional add-on (not included in base estimate).
- Risk: Network restrictions prevent outbound failover -> Mitigation: Use air-gapped config with local caching; remote log export optional after negotiation.

Next steps / actions required to start:
- Customer signature on SOW and acceptance of payment milestones.
- Delivery of validation dataset and access information for staging hosts.
- Scheduling of initial 3 discovery workshops (preferred dates within next 2 weeks).

Point of contact (Redwood):
- Aisha Patel, Solutions Engineer (owner) — aisha@redwood.ai — +1-415-555-0182

Appendices (brief):
A) Validation dataset spec: minimum 1,500 labeled frames, balanced across defect classes, include edge-case lighting conditions.
B) Minimum POC host requirements: 1 x NVIDIA A10/A30 class GPU, 64GB RAM, 500GB NVMe, Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL8 compatible, open egress to Redwood control plane for telemetry (or explicit air-gapped config to be planned).

Notes and internal flags (engineering):
- Consider recommending int8 quantization profile and batch size 8 default for inference path to achieve latency targets; need kernel test on A30 to confirm.
- Plan for simple fallback degradation mode to return 'deferred-inspect' events to MES when external capacity unavailable.
- Follow up with SRE for observability retention limits for POC dashboard exports.

This is a draft SOW intended to be iterated with customer security and ops teams; pricing and estimates will be finalized after discovery workshops.
